simple.meaning: לָקַשׁ (lâqash) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to gather the after crop.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Job, beginning at Job 24:6. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לָקַשׁ (H3953) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: לָקַשׁ (lâqash) / H3953 is traced through Job 24:6 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H3953. laqash [ לָקַשׁ ] verb only Pi`el 3masculine plural, probably denominative from לֶקֶשׁ = take the aftermath , i.e. take everything (Wetzst in De Hiob 26, 6 ) (> Buhl II. לקשׁ , compare Arabic schnell zusammenraffen [compare Lane 2668 ]); — despoil ; ׃ יְלֵַקּשׁוּ רָשָׁע וְכֶרֶם Job 24:6 and the vineyard of the wicked (but read probably עָשִׁיר the rich Bu Du) they despoil (|| קָצַר ). לשׁד (√ of following, compare Arabic suck, lick (Ethiopic butter ); so Thes and on Psa 32:4 De Bae, also Di Num 11:8 ).
